item.title: [github_trending] alibaba/open-code-review
item.description: Alibaba has open-sourced OpenCodeReview, a Go code-review tool that combines deterministic pipelines with an LLM agent to produce precise line-level comments, supported by a built-in multi-language ruleset covering issues such as NPEs and thread safety. It is described as battle-tested at Alibaba's scale, making it worth a look for teams wiring automated review into CI without trusting an LLM for every judgement.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A developer recounts moving from Cursor to OpenAI Codex: after about a year on Cursor, starting with a $20/month personal plan in April 2025, his company switched its China region to Codex in April 2026, partly because Cursor moved from fixed licensing to usage-based billing that made costs higher and less predictable. His main takeaway is a difference in form: Cursor reads as an IDE with AI attached, while Codex feels closer to a general-purpose agent.

item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, a model aimed at coding, computer use, professional workflows, and cybersecurity, scoring 72.6% on OSWorld 2.0 against 65.7% for GPT-5.6 Sol. It supports a 1M-token context, adds an experimental context mechanism in Codex, and is the first OpenAI model classified as having "critical cybersecurity capability"; it is rolling out to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise, plus API, Azure, and AWS Bedrock users.

item.title: [infoq] OpenAI故意欠技术债，等Codex来还：仅2名工程师，把核心存储从Python重写成Rust
item.description: OpenAI deliberately took on technical debt by building Habitat, its core online storage platform, as a Python service, betting that Codex and GPT would eventually make a rewrite cheap. In the second quarter of this year, two engineers rewrote it in Rust with Codex and GPT-5.5; the Rust version now handles 95% of production requests with 6x better CPU efficiency, 15x better memory efficiency, and lower average and tail latency.

It uses low-latency communication and AMOLED variable-refresh-rate power optimizations, supports themes, and the code lives at reycn/tars on GitHub.

item.description: Cloudflare has moved cdnjs, which serves roughly 9 billion requests a day, off its mixed Cloudflare and Google Cloud publishing stack and onto its own developer platform, making R2 the authoritative source for published files while Workers, Workflows and KV handle package ingestion. Existing URLs, package contents and SRI hashes are preserved. Cloudflare frames it as dogfooding its platform at public-service scale; cdnjs reports a 98.6% cache hit rate and is used by about 12% of websites.

item.description: Ghidra is a software reverse engineering framework built and maintained by the National Security Agency's Research Directorate. Users can extend it with Java or Python, making it a customizable platform for malware analysis and large-team SRE work.
